title: Unpack the Delivery
story:
Tomasz: The Petrel delivered `glacier.tar.gz` from the mainland lab. Forty years of glacier-front measurements.
Ingrid: Where is it?
Tomasz: In `/workspace/incoming`. I cannot simply extract it on the host. The permissions on the old server were a swamp, and the viewer containers expect it in a Docker volume.

Ingrid: Then make it a volume, engineer. There is a `MANIFEST.sha256` inside. Nobody tells Tomasz it is done until the checksums pass.
objectives: Extract `/workspace/incoming/glacier.tar.gz` into it using a throwaway container (the tarball must stay in place)
`sha256sum -c MANIFEST.sha256` inside the volume must report every file `OK`
startingState: The tarball `/workspace/incoming/glacier.tar.gz` exists. No volume called `glacier-data` exists yet.
hints: Restoring is the reverse of backing up: a helper container mounts the target volume and the folder with the tarball, and unpacks one into the other.
Mount the volume at `/data` and `/workspace/incoming` at `/incoming` (read-only is fine), then run `tar xzf /incoming/glacier.tar.gz -C /data`.

```bash
docker run --rm \
  -v glacier-data:/data \
  -v /workspace/incoming:/incoming:ro \
  alpine:3.20 tar xzf /incoming/glacier.tar.gz -C /data
docker run --rm -v glacier-data:/data alpine:3.20 \
  sh -c 'cd /data && sha256sum -c MANIFEST.sha256'
```

commands: mkdir -p incoming && d=$(mktemp -d) && for i in 1 2 3; do head -c 2048 /dev/urandom | base64 > $d/core-000$i.dat; done && (cd $d && sha256sum *.dat > MANIFEST.sha256) && tar czf incoming/glacier.tar.gz -C $d . && rm -rf $d

params.command: docker run --rm -v glacier-data:/data alpine:3.20 sh -c 'cd /data && sha256sum -c MANIFEST.sha256'

validation.description: Every file in `glacier-data` passes the manifest (`sha256sum -c MANIFEST.sha256`)
The delivered tarball `incoming/glacier.tar.gz` is still in place

solution: docker run --rm -v glacier-data:/data -v /workspace/incoming:/incoming:ro alpine:3.20 tar xzf /incoming/glacier.tar.gz -C /data
debrief: Restoring a volume is just extracting an archive into it through a helper container; the volume does not care how its files arrived. Pro tip: verify a restore with a checksum manifest, because a tarball that extracts without error can still be incomplete.
